# Rational lifting through the subgroup generated by `U(χ)`, `χ` and `U(χ⁻¹)`

Author: Worker 37.

This module proves rational lifting for quotients by dynamic parabolics over
infinite fields, and from it the infinite-field, trivial-split-radical case of
the published pseudo-parabolic rational-lifting property. Both results work at
an arbitrary universe `u`.

## `Dynamic.rational_lifts_of_infinite`

Hypotheses:

- `k` is an infinite field and `G` is a smooth affine group scheme over `k`
  with connected underlying space;
- `i : P ⟶ G` is a closed subgroup whose all-test range is `P(χ)` for a
  cocharacter `χ` (`hχ : SubgroupFunctor.range i = Dynamic.parabolic χ`);
- `q : G.X ⟶ Q` is a supplied quotient: `Q` is separated, quasi-compact and
  locally of finite type over `k`, `q` is smooth, surjective and
  quasi-compact, and on every relative test `T`, `a ≫ q = b ≫ q` if and only if
  `a⁻¹ * b` lies in the range of `i`.

Conclusion: every rational point `p` of `Q` has a rational point `g` of `G`
with `g ≫ q = p`.

Proof. Let `D` be the smooth connected closed subgroup generated by
`(a, t, b) ↦ a · χ(t) · b` on `U(χ) ×_k 𝔾_m ×_k U(χ⁻¹)`
(`OppositeEnvelope.exists_generatedImage`). The stabilizer `P` is smooth, by
the published `HomogeneousQuotient.smooth_subgroup_of_smooth_quotient`.

1. The range of `D.inclusion` is normalized by `P(χ)`, which is the range of
   `i` (`OppositeEnvelope.isNormalizedBy_parabolic`), and it contains `U(χ⁻¹)`
   (`OppositeEnvelope.reversed_unipotent_le`). By
   `normalized_subgroup_product_smooth_surjective` the multiplication
   `D.group ×_k P ⟶ G` is smooth and surjective.
2. The image of `χ` lies in `D` (`OppositeEnvelope.range_cocharacter_le`), so
   `χ` factors as `ψ ≫ D.inclusion` for an actual cocharacter `ψ` of `D.group`.
   By the published `parabolic_eq_comap_of_isClosedSubgroup`, `P(ψ)` is the
   full preimage of `P(χ)` in `D.group`; its affine representative is
   `j = Affine.parabolicHom ψ`.
3. The published `HomogeneousQuotientRestriction.restrict`, fed the smooth
   surjective multiplication of step 1, makes the same target `Q`, with
   projection `D.inclusion ≫ q`, a homogeneous quotient of `D.group` by `j`.
   It has the exact right-coset fibre condition on every relative test.
4. Over the infinite field `k`, `D.group` has dense rational points
   (`OppositeEnvelope.hasDenseRationalPoints`). The published
   `rational_lifts_of_dense_parabolic` uses an identity section of the
   quotient built from the opposite dynamic cell. Applied to `D.group`, `ψ`,
   `j` and the restricted projection, it gives a rational point `d` of
   `D.group` with `d ≫ D.inclusion ≫ q = p`. The asserted lift is
   `g = d ≫ D.inclusion`.

## `OppositeEnvelopeLifting.property_of_trivial_split_radical`

Over an infinite field `k`, let `G` be smooth, affine and connected, and let
`n : N ⟶ G` be a split ground-field unipotent radical
(`IsSplitUnipotentRadical n`) with trivial all-test range. Then `G` has the
published `PseudoParabolicRationalLiftingProperty`. That is, every rational
point of every supplied quotient of `G` by any pseudo-parabolic subgroup
lifts to a rational point of `G`, with exactly the quotient hypotheses of the
property.

Proof. The published product theorem `pseudoParabolicSplitRadicalProduct`
supplies the product replacement needed by
`DynamicParabolicPresentation.ofSplitProduct`. Because the split radical is
trivial, that construction gives an actual cocharacter `χ` with
`SubgroupFunctor.range i = Dynamic.parabolic χ`. The theorem
`Dynamic.rational_lifts_of_infinite` then applies to the original `i`, `Q` and
`q`.

## Provenance

This implements the infinite-field case of the rational-point conclusion of
Conrad–Gabber–Prasad, *Pseudo-reductive groups*, second edition (2015),
Lemma C.2.1 (printed pp.592–593; source ID
`conrad-gabber-prasad-2015-pseudo-reductive`). The reduction to trivial split
radical and the use of the opposite cell follow the outline recorded in the
published Markdown of `PseudoParabolicQuotientRationalLiftingStatement`. The
implemented route differs from that outline in one respect. The subgroup
generated by ground-field tori is replaced by the subgroup generated by
`U(χ)`, `χ` and `U(χ⁻¹)`, which needs only normalization by `P(χ)` rather than
normality in `G`. The restriction and density-lifting steps are the same
published interfaces used by the conditional torus-envelope route
`TorusGeneratedEnvelope.rational_lifts_dynamic`.
